nodes.name: ZIF-67 Growth on Ni Foam
nodes.procedure: thick and uniform ZIF-67 nanorod (with an average length and diameter of ≈4.5 μm and 300 and 200 nm) arrays were vertically grown on the nickel foam (Figure S1, Supporting Information) in ambient condition.
nodes.source_text: First, thick and uniform ZIF-67 nanorod ... arrays were vertically grown on the nickel foam ... in ambient condition.

nodes.name: Ion Exchange to Ru-CoNi-LDH
nodes.procedure: the solid ZIF-67 nanorod arrays were used as the templates and transformed into Ru-CoNi-LDH nanosheets assembled nanotubes in the nickel nitrate and ruthenium chloride solution. During the reaction process, the presence of water in the pores of ZIF-67 and protons generated from the hydrolysis of Ni2+ and Ru3+ could gradually consume the ZIF-67 to release the Co2+ ions into the solution. Meanwhile, some released Co2+ ions were oxidized to Co3+ by dissolved O2 and NO3- ions in the solution, and the Co3+ ions coprecipitate with Ni2+/Co2+/Ru3+ to form a hierarchical shell constructed Ru-CoNi-LDH nanosheets at the surface of the ZIF-67 precursors. Then, the nanosheets continue to grow with the dissolution of the inner ZIF-67. Under steady control of the solvent composition and Ni2+ and Ru3+ ion concentrations, well-defined hierarchical Ru-CoNi-LDH hollow nanotubes could finally be obtained as seen from the TEM image in Figure S3d.
nodes.source_text: Then, the solid ZIF-67 nanorod arrays were used as the templates and transformed into Ru-CoNi-LDH nanosheets assembled nanotubes in the nickel nitrate and ruthenium chloride solution as shown in Figure S3 ... well-defined hierarchical Ru-CoNi-LDH hollow nanotubes could finally be obtained.

nodes.name: Air Plasma Treatment
nodes.procedure: after air-plasma treatment, the nanotube arrays do not appear obvious change as seen from the SEM and TEM images in Figure 1b,c. However, the nanosheets became distinct rough and porous as displayed in Figure 1d which caused by the erosion effect of air plasma. The air plasma treatment not only introduce N and O filling into the superfluous Vo in Ru-CoNi-LDH but also greatly improve the surface hydrophilicity.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows hollow nanotube arrays of P-Ru-CoNi-LDH with rough and porous nanosheets after air-plasma treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the nanotube arrays do not appear obvious change as seen from the SEM and TEM images in Figure 1b,c. However, the nanosheets became distinct rough and porous as displayed in Figure 1d

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows lattice fringes with distances of 0.228 and 0.238 nm corresponding to crystalline phase of P-Ru-CoNi-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM graph in Figure 1e detected the lattice fringes with distance of 0.228 and 0.238 nm which was in accordance with the crystalline phase before plasma.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Co, Ni, Ru, O, and N species in P-Ru-CoNi-LDH with N at 3.41 atom%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the elemental mapping images from energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) showed a homogeneous distribution of Co, Ni, Ru, O, and N species (Figure 1f–k). The arisen N element with a 3.41% atom ratio

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 855.5 and 873.1 eV for Ni2+, Co 2p for Co2+/Co3+, Ru 3p at 463.3 and 485.8 eV for Ru3+, with shifts indicating electronic interactions and oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS in Figure 2 and Figures S11-S13 in the Supporting Information further finely illustrated the electronic interactions between the atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR spectra show increased oxygen vacancy concentration (g=1.999) in Ru-CoNi-LDH compared to CoNi-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra in Figure 2d were conducted to analyze the concentration of oxygen vacancies (g = 1.999) qualitatively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Water and 1M KOH contact angles of 0° for P-Ru-CoNi-LDH indicate superhydrophilicity; H2 contact angle of 150° indicates supraerophobicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: when P-Ru-CoNi-LDH, Ru-CoNi-LDH, P-CoNi-LDH, and CoNi-LDH touched with 1 M KOH electrolyte and deionized water (DI water) in air, the liquid drops were quickly spread out ... H2 bubble touched the P-Ru-CoNi-LDH/nickel foam (NF) surface, the bubble remained spherical and nonsticking with a contact angle of 150°

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines electrochemical double-layer capacitances: P-Ru-CoNi-LDH 16.1 mF cm^-2, P-CoNi-LDH 22.1 mF cm^-2, Ru-CoNi-LDH 5.79 mF cm^-2, CoNi-LDH 7.27 mF cm^-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Cdl values of Ru-CoNi-LDH, CoNi-LDH, P-Ru-CoNi-LDH, and P-CoNi-LDH were determined to be 5.79, 7.27, 16.1, and 22.1 mF cm^-2, respectively (calculated based on corresponding CV curves in Figure S18, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows smallest Nyquist plot radius for P-Ru-CoNi-LDH, indicating highest electrical conductivity and fastest electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) performed in Figure 4e was conducted to contrast the radii of the curves ... The smallest radius of P-Ru-CoNi-LDH revealed a higher electrical conductivity

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows strongest H-O-H peaks at 1650 cm^-1 and 3500 cm^-1 for P-Ru-CoNi-LDH, indicating best water adsorption capacity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ Raman spectra were carried out during the HER process as displayed in Figure 6a-e ... P-Ru-CoNi-LDH displayed the strongest peak intensity at ≈1650 cm^-1 (ω H-O-H) and ≈3500 cm^-1 (Interfacial water)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns match (003), (006), (012), (113) facets of CoNi-LDH (PDF#40-0216); (003) peak shifts to lower 2θ with Ru doping; peaks broaden after plasma treatment indicating smaller crystallite size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XRD patterns of the as prepared samples ... all the characteristic peaks matched well to (003), (006), (012), and (113) facets of CoNi-LDH (PDF# 40-0216) ... gradual trend of the (003) diffraction peaks shifted to lower 2θ values ... diffraction peaks gradually broaden and weak with the increasing of Ru contend
